summary: Grandma's childhood by the sea, war and peace, the history of Starlight House, life and society, and an old photograph.

scene.ko: 할머니, 어린 시절 이야기 해 주세요.
scene.en: Grandma, tell me about when you were little.

scene.ko: 할머니는 천구백오십사 년에 강릉에서 태어났어. 그 무렵에는 다 가난했어.
scene.en: I was born in 1954 in Gangneung. Back then, everyone was poor.

scene.ko: 우리 집은 농사를 지었어. 아버지는 농업을 하셨고, 어머니는 소하고 닭을 기르셨어.
scene.en: Our family farmed. My father worked the land, and my mother raised cows and chickens.
b: to make, to cook (rice), to build

scene.ko: 할머니도 일했어요?
scene.en: Did you work too?

scene.ko: 그럼. 어린 나이에 동생들을 키웠어. 엄마가 아이를 여섯 명 낳으셨거든. 고생을 많이 했지.
scene.en: Of course. I raised my little brothers and sisters while I was young myself. My mother had six children, you see. It was a hard life.

scene.ko: 배고프면 바닷가에서 고구마를 구워 먹곤 했어. 정말 맛있었어.
scene.en: When we were hungry, we'd roast sweet potatoes on the beach. They were so good.
b: to grill, to bake, to roast

scene.ko: 그런 어려움 속에서 어떻게 자랐어요?
scene.en: How did you grow up through such hardship?
b: to be how (어때요? = how is it?)

scene.ko: 우리 때는 모두 힘들게 자라났어. 육십 년대, 칠십 년대에는 다 고생했어. 그래서 지금이 고마워.
scene.en: Everyone in our day grew up the hard way. In the sixties and seventies, everyone struggled. That's why I'm grateful for now.
b: to have a hard time, to work hard

scene.ko: 이야기를 들으니까 눈물이 어려요.
scene.en: Hearing this, my eyes are filling with tears.

scene.ko: 아이고, 울지 마. 다 고생한 덕분에 이 집이 있는 거야.
scene.en: Oh, don't cry. All that hard work is why we have this house.

notes.title: -곤 하다
notes.text: -곤 했어요 describes something you did again and again in the past: 바다에서 놀곤 했어요 (I'd often play by the sea). It sounds warm and nostalgic — perfect for storytelling. 고생 많이 하셨어요 ("you've been through so much") is a deeply kind thing to say to an elder.

scene.en: Grandma, it's history homework. What was the Korean War?

notes.title: A divided peninsula
notes.text: The Korean War (1950–1953) left the peninsula divided into South Korea (대한민국) and North Korea (북한), and many families were separated. Peace (평화) and reunification (통일) remain deeply emotional topics, especially for older Koreans like Grandma.

lessons.goal: Say what used to be true with -았/었었-.

notes.title: -았/었었-
notes.text: The double past -았/었었- says something was true before but isn't anymore: 학생이 많았었어요 (there used to be many students — not now), 별이가 살았었어요 (Byeol used to live there). 사람 부자 ("rich in people") is a lovely way to say someone is surrounded by loved ones.

lessons.goal: Talk about society, the world and life.

notes.title: -적
notes.text: The suffix -적 turns nouns into "-al / -ic" words: 정치 (politics) → 정치적 (political), 사회 (society) → 사회적 (social), 세계 (world) → 세계적 (world-class), 역사 → 역사적 (historic). Before a noun, add 인: 정치적인 이야기 (political talk).

notes.title: -(으)ㄴ 채로
notes.text: -(으)ㄴ 채로 means "with (something) still as it is": 사진을 든 채로 잠들었어요 (fell asleep still holding the photo), 신발을 신은 채로 (with your shoes still on — never in a Korean home!). 우리말 ("our language") is how Koreans fondly refer to Korean.
